hub.reportTitle: State of public IT and creative procurement
hub.reportText: A quarterly report on what governments buy in these categories, how much and from whom. The first issue publishes once two quarters of data are collected.
framing: Governments in Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia publish their tenders and contract awards as open data. Each country uses its own portal and its own codes, so the same kind of work, such as database design or brand materials, is listed under different names in each place. This section brings those notices together under 13 plain categories that match the services Awesoon delivers.

Every night the pages read the official feeds: CanadaBuys, USAspending, Contracts Finder and Find a Tender, and AusTender. A notice is matched to a category by its classification codes, never by guessing from the title. Counts, medians and charts are worked out from those records only, and each block names its source, its licence and when it was last updated.

Use it to see which buyers post your kind of work, what contracts usually cost the buyer, and what is closing soon. Awesoon is a Vancouver firm led by founder Ray Rasouli. If a notice fits what we deliver, we are glad to partner or bid.

category.capText: One page with our services, codes, registrations and contacts for public sector buyers.
faq: Where does this data come from?
From {sources}, read every night. Each block on this page names its source, its licence and when it was last updated.
How is a notice put in this category?
By its official classification codes, such as UNSPSC, CPV, NAICS or PSC, matched against the codes for {category}. Titles are never used to guess.
What does the median award value mean?
Half of the awards with a stated value in the last 12 months were above it and half below. It is the value of the contract to the buyer, not a price Awesoon charges.
Can Awesoon bid on or partner for these tenders?
Yes, where the work fits what we deliver. Ray Rasouli reviews each notice himself. Book a call or email the notice reference.
framing: This page tracks every public notice {countryIn} that is coded as {category}. It shows the tenders open today, the awards made in the last 12 months and the buyers who post this work most often. The numbers are worked out each night from the official records, with no estimates added, so a quiet month shows as a quiet month.

Public buyers rarely post this work under one name. One department calls it a modernization, another a support contract, a third a framework. Classification codes are what tie them together, which is why the category here follows the codes and not the wording of the title. Values are what the buyer agreed to pay the supplier, in the local currency, and some notices do not state a value at all.

Suppliers use this page to judge whether a category is worth bidding on, to find buyers to introduce themselves to, and to see typical contract sizes before pricing. Buyers use it to see what similar organisations have bought and from whom.

framing: This profile gathers every contract award and open tender that {buyer} has published in the 13 categories Awesoon follows, from IT and ERP work to design and advertising. It shows how often they buy, which categories they buy in and what a typical contract is worth to them. Every number comes from the official open data for {country} and is refreshed each night.

A buyer that posts the same kind of work several times a year is usually a better first conversation than a one-off notice. The recent awards table shows who won each contract, which helps a supplier see whether the buyer prefers large firms, frameworks or smaller specialists.

Names here are exactly as the buyer wrote them in the feed, so the same department can appear under two spellings. Values are in the local currency and are the contract value to the buyer, not anyone's price. Profiles with fewer than five awards stay out of search until there is enough history to be useful.

framing: Each week this page lists the new public tenders and contract awards {countryIn} in the 13 categories Awesoon follows: IT expert services, ERP and CRM work, programming, database design, interface work, game software, staffing, and advertising and design. It covers the last seven days and is rebuilt every night from the official feeds.

It is meant for small suppliers who cannot read every portal every day. Scan the titles, open the official notice for the ones that fit, and check the closing date before you plan a bid. Tenders that close soon are worth reading first. Values are shown in the local currency when the buyer states one.

The email version will send the same list each Monday to people who ask for it. Consent is always opt-in, the box starts unticked, and you can leave with one click. Until the mailing list is live, signing up simply opens an email to Ray Rasouli, and this site keeps nothing.

report.title: State of public IT and creative procurement
report.placeholder: The first issue publishes once two full quarters of data are collected. Collection started in {first}.
framing: Each quarter this report will sum up how governments in Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia buy IT, ERP, CRM, database, design and advertising work. It compares the number of awards, typical contract values and the most active buyers across the four countries, using only the official open data each country publishes.

It needs two full quarters before it can show a change rather than a single snapshot, so it stays a placeholder until then. Every figure in it will name its source and licence, and the method will be written out so anyone can check the numbers.

Journalists, researchers and procurement teams are welcome to cite it with a link. Questions about the method go to founder Ray Rasouli, who reads every message himself. The report does not replace the official notices. It is a way to spot trends, and every notice should still be read on the country's own portal before anyone decides to bid.
